scores.Biological Plausibility_reason: CAF-derived TGF-β signaling through TGFBR–SMAD and p21/p27-mediated RB/E2F suppression is a biologically defensible mechanism for reduced proliferation and Ki-67. TGF-β responses in breast cancer are context-dependent, so its proposed dominance and vessel-distance relationship remain hypotheses rather than established conclusions.
scores.Grounded Mechanistic Synthesis_reason: The response integrates CAF-derived TGFB1, tumor TGFBR1/2–SMAD2/3 signaling, p21/p27-mediated CDK inhibition, RB/E2F–FOXM1 suppression, and reduced Ki-67 into a coherent spatial mechanism. FAP, ACTA2, PDGFRB, SERPINE1, JUNB, and SKIL function mainly as state or source markers rather than mechanistic intermediates, and the vessel-distance component is not fully connected. No synthesis ceiling was applied because the principal focus-to-target mechanism is explicit, multistep, and biologically resolved.
